items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — went straight from confirming the name into pulling up the quote
No agenda statement ('I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes — sound good?') before diving into the recap
No explicit 'sound good?' confirmation anywhere in the call

Didn't probe additional rooms (garage/storage unit/balcony), narrow hallways or long-walk concerns, storage stops, additional stops, or ask a moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000) never mentioned
Meet Your Mover program (photo/info email before move day) never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned, even though an arrival window (12:30-2:30 PM) was given
No school-bus-style equivalent used to make the 3.5-4.5 hour estimate concrete
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no mention that consolidating small items or taking a carload shortens the move and lowers the bill
No confirmation/quote email mentioned at all, even though Andrew needs to confirm his building's freight elevator before booking
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' at the close
No stated office hours or way to reach the team beyond this call
Used Andrew's name only once ('Andrew Smith, right?') across the call, not 3+ times
No insurance walkthrough (No Worries + 60¢/lb baseline) and no proactive rapport-building moment beyond routine affirmations
top_strength: Jules quickly recovered a lost online quote lead, efficiently re-confirmed all the move details already on file, and delivered a clear, accurate hourly-rate estimate with a solid no-hidden-fees pitch and clock explanation, all inside a tight 6.3-minute call.
coaching_note: Build the three missing differentiators — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee — into the pricing walkthrough, and don't skip the Save Your Ass prep speech before wrapping; none of the four were mentioned on this call even though pricing, the clock, and the estimate were all covered well.
phone_presence_notes: Jules was polite and responsive with routine affirmations ('Got it,' 'No problem,' 'Awesome'), but stayed largely transactional — Andrew's name was used only once and there was no small talk or rapport beyond the task itself.
